analysis: Examined all units. (1) Darkbloom.swift:178-229 and StartCommand+Modes.swift:216-217: the registration weight hash for models with weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad can now come from a VerifiedWeightHashStore record, read from disk at VerifiedWeightHashStore.path(), when file identities match. Before, every startup hash was recomputed from the actual bytes. This touches T-012/T-027/A-004 and the SEC-007 fail-open context under TB-003/ADV-001. The operator controls the filesystem and may be able to forge the record file. Whether file identities (inode/size/mtime?) can be spoofed after an in-place weight edit is not visible here. The comment at line 220 says the managed load SHA-256-verifies every file before serving. If that holds against a trusted manifest, any substitution is caught at load and the registration hash stays advisory. That would be a safe direction, consistent with the existing fingerprint-before-hash ordering (lines 188-192). Neither of the following is visible in this batch: VerifiedWeightHashStore (record format, file permissions, identity fields, integrity) and the managed-load verification reference source. Also unknown: whether the model_hashes signed in status challenges (TB-009 StatusCanonical) reuse these registration hashes for a model that has not been loaded since the record was written. Integration should confirm that the managed load verifies against an independent manifest, not the record. It should also confirm that a forged or stale record cannot make attested status report a hash the served bytes do not match. No finding is raised because the contract is outside the supplied evidence. (2) GLMWiredLimitAdvice.swift (new) and DoctorCommand.swift:82-87,107-111 add a read-only doctor warn/pass check plus a printed sysctl/LaunchDaemon guide. Model IDs from config and daemon state are only matched by predicate. The recommendation strings come from ProviderCore GLM5NextWiredLimit, which is not shown. The check is deliberately kept out of buildDoctorChecks/verify. No trust, attestation, encryption or admission effect was identified. The advice suggests root sysctl/LaunchDaemon commands for the operator to paste. The generated text should be confirmed to be static constants, not derived from untrusted input.
